assumptions.statement: V1 uses Supernote Cloud download/upload only and does not write through the local Partner App sync folder.
assumptions.validation: Confirmed in approved design spec and user discussion.

assumptions.statement: The first safe implementation slice is a read-only snapshot browser foundation before write-capable reorder.
assumptions.validation: Matches the approved staged design and reduces device-corruption risk.

assumptions.statement: Page IDs are stable enough to serve as canonical identity during same-notebook reorder.
assumptions.validation: Validate with unit tests and fixture/manual device tests before enabling write operations broadly.

decision_log.decision: Use Speedrift with PlanForge-seeded Workgraph and TDD loops.
evidence: User asked to build with Speedrift and testing loops.
decision_log.reason: The user explicitly requested Speedrift and testing loops.

evidence: User said to hold custom shape/sticker marker idea until later.
decision_log.reason: User asked to hold that idea until later; V1 uses native metadata only.

decision_log.decision: Start with read model and APIs before write-capable reorder.
evidence: Approved design spec stages read-only browser before metadata-aware reorder and cross-note move.
decision_log.reason: Metadata preservation and validation are the main risk; read-only snapshot code enables fixtures and UI without upload risk.

acceptance_criteria: Backend can build a NotebookSnapshot from .note bytes keyed by page_id.
Snapshot exposes page order, page records, stars, headings/titles, keywords, links, and image dimensions without mutating notebooks.
Backend has tested image rendering/cache primitives suitable for a page grid.
A minimal local web UI can display a notebook page grid with zoom and metadata filters.
Same-notebook reorder engine exists behind tests but blocks unsafe metadata rather than risking lossy writes.
All implementation tasks run Speedrift drift checks and focused pytest/UX checks.
end_state.contract: Implement the first Speedrift execution slice of the Supernote Cloud Page Organizer: read-only snapshot/browser foundation plus tested metadata-aware reorder groundwork, preserving the approved cloud-side design constraints.
out_of_scope: Custom shape or sticker marker detection.
Automatic merge of stale cloud snapshots.

fix_loops.action: Use TDD red-green-refactor for the focused failing behavior, then re-run the task verify command.
fix_loops.escalation: If the same test class fails after three attempts, stop and create a replanning/fix task.
fix_loops.trigger: Focused test failure inside a Workgraph task.

fix_loops.action: Capture advisory drift findings as follow-up tasks unless they directly invalidate the current task contract.
fix_loops.escalation: If drift indicates scope expansion beyond the touch set, update the graph rather than silently editing extra files.

goal: Build the Supernote Cloud Page Organizer with Speedrift and testing loops, after updating Speedrift tooling.

artifacts: new organizer backend/UI modules and focused tests
handoff.completion_policy: Complete only after Workgraph tasks for the selected slice pass focused tests, drift checks have run, and remaining risks are recorded as follow-up tasks.

model_assignments.reason: Default Speedrift execution route for coding and test loops.
Browser/product UX checks require the standard Codex route with local browser tooling when needed.
Review and drift interpretation should use the same registry-backed execution surface unless policy says otherwise.

risks.mitigation: Block write-capable reorder for unsupported link metadata until fixture and device validation prove safe remapping.
risks.risk: Supernote link metadata may need more than page-number remapping.

risks.mitigation: Keep Phase 1 read-only and add golden fixtures before writes.
risks.risk: supernotelib reconstruction may omit or normalize metadata in ways that only appear on device.

risks.mitigation: Scope commits carefully and avoid touching unrelated dirty files unless required.
risks.risk: The repository currently has unrelated uncommitted changes.
